articles.title: New Batman: Part 2 Set Photos Hint at the Court of Owls
articles.summary: New videos and photos from the London set of The Batman: Part II show Robert Pattinson’s Bruce Wayne being escorted by police through a crowd of angry protestors. These images only further fuel the rumors that Gotham’s secret cabal of wealthy elites, the Court of Owls, factor into the story, but…
body: Footage on social media shows director Matt Reeves and cinematographer Erik Messerschmidt filming a scene where Bruce is protected by the GCPD as he exits down the stairs of the Gotham Bar Association past mobs of protestors to a waiting Bentley where he’s met by Andy Serkis’ double as Alfred Pennyworth. (Serkis is busy in New Zealand directing and starring in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.) Jeffrey Wright as Jim Gordon was also spotted on set.

The signs and placards waved by the protestors’ reveal the source of their anger and the first hint of the Court of Owls: “ Court of Oligarchs,” “Court of Fouls,” “The Richer Get Richer,” “One Day The Poor Will Have Nothing,” “ Re$i$t,” “Eat the Rich,” “Your Greed is Killin Us,” and “Oligarchs Gotta Go!.”
There are also signs bearing Batman imagery, such as one that reads “ Save Us ” and another that features the Batman mask with “I’m coming for you next” written below it.

The irony in these images, of course, is that the protesters clearly view Bruce Wayne, the city’s wealthiest man, as an enemy while embracing his alter ego Batman as a symbol of resistance against a corrupt system.

articles.title: Diablo 5 Director Confirms Game is Already in Full Production
articles.summary: Diablo 5 is officially in full production and coming in 2029. Game Director Joe Shely reveals the sequel will feature more classes, procedural worlds, and jump 100 years into the future.
body: While tons of new updates are coming to Diablo, including a new Netflix series, Diablo 4 Season 15, a Switch 2 port, and more, the biggest reveal for the franchise at BlizzCon 2026 was the announcement of Diablo V, coming in 2029.

IGN sat down exclusively with the team behind the upcoming game, including Game Director Joe Shely, Narrative Director Jennifer Helper, and Production Director Tiffany Wat, who gave us tons of new details about Diablo 5, including how it’s already past early development.
IGN: I know probably nobody has missed the Diablo 5 announcement, but can you guys just kind of give sort of a top-level view of what the game will be?

Joe Shely: Diablo 5 is a world where Sanctuary has fallen and Diablo has won. That means that the world is in an apocalypse. The fate that players have been trying to prevent for many years throughout other Diablo games has happened. Other heroes rose up, tried to stop Diablo, and failed. Diablo sits on the throne of Westmarch and has conquered all of the Western continent.
points: Diablo 5 is officially in full production and coming in 2029.
Game Director Joe Shely reveals the sequel will feature more classes, procedural worlds, and jump 100 years into the future.

articles.title: You’ll Fight The Protoss In StarCraft, Too, Don’t Worry
articles.summary: StarCraft's reveal trailer squarely put the focus on the Terrans, who later in the cinematic face a terrifying confrontation with the Zerg. The franchise's three franchises--including the Protoss--have always been a central element of what distinguishes StarCraft from other strategy games.
body: GameSpot spoke with GM and creative director Dan Hay at BlizzCon and asked him about how the three factions will interact with each other. Although he was expectedly coy on specifics, he did offer up some thoughts.

"The answer to that question is I absolutely unequivocally can't say," Hay said. "But what I can do is tell you what I would want as a player. I'll hint at sort of not what we're doing, but some of the things that we think about.

"Of course, what you want to be able to do... you think about the Protoss and how reverent we are. They're older, and there's a mystique and a grandness to them, right? They have just a completely different flavor. Then you have the Zerg, and the Zerg are just numberless; they're infinite from the standpoint of they just overwhelm you with sheer organic power. Then you have the Terrans, that are this group of... they're working their way through the sector in kind of a haphazard and industrial way. We want that feeling.
points: StarCraft's reveal trailer squarely put the focus on the Terrans, who later in the cinematic face a terrifying confrontation with the Zerg.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Geralt Skin for Diablo 4 Barbarians Revealed — but There's a Catch
articles.summary: CD Projekt and Blizzard have released a first look at the Geralt-themed Barbarian skin for Diablo 4, but you'll need to preorder The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on Battle.net to get it.
body: During BlizzCon 2026, CD Projekt’s Expert Community and Social Media Manager Amelia Korzycka and Level Design Lead Miles Tost appeared as guests on the 30 Years of Battle.net panel to reveal the skin, which will be available to Battle.net players who pre-purchase Songs of the Past (it’s only available to wishlist right now), or buy the expansion when it launches. That means the Geralt skin is locked behind Battle.net, which in turn means Steam players, for example, miss out.

This, as you can imagine, isn’t going down particularly well with Diablo 4 players who already own The Witcher 3 on non-Battle.net platforms. Remastered is coming to Steam as a free upgrade on September 29, 2026 for anyone who already owns the base game. So, those who already own The Witcher 3 on Steam (at this point, who doesn't?) and are interested in Songs of the Past are probably going to buy it on Valve's platform, and probably don't want to rebuy The Witcher 3 on Battle.net just so they can get the Geralt skin for Diablo 4.
“Not paying for a second copy of a 15-year-old game that most people who would play it probably already own,” one person said on social media. “Thx though Blizzard.”

articles.title: ‘Hell Yes!’ - Diablo 4 Dev Team Reacts to the Franchise’s New Netflix Show
articles.summary: Among the many announcements during yesterday’s BlizzCon Opening Ceremony, the news that Diablo is getting its own show at Netflix has at least one of the franchise’s development teams chomping at the bit.
body: Regardless, the development team behind Diablo 4 says it’s quite possibly the reveal they are most excited about, even more so than the news that Diablo 5 is coming out in 2029, Diablo 4 is getting a Switch 2 port, Spawn is coming to Diablo Immortal, and the arrival of the Amazon class. I sat down with Brent Gibson, Diablo 4’s Game Director, and Owen Leach, Season Lead for Diablo 4 - Hell’s Legacy, after yesterday’s news to break everything down.

“Even though I have no information and can't share anything, the fact that we're getting a show [is what I’m most excited about]," Gibson says. “I'm a story guy. I want to see more story, as much story as you can get. We’re narrowing in on finding the creative team [for the show] and we're delivering on what Johanna was saying, [that] we're Blizzard Entertainment. I think Diablo's a perfect world to start telling those stories, so I couldn't be more happy that we're getting a show.”

articles.title: The StarCraft Shooter Is A Third-Person Game, And Blizzard Insists That You Have To Feel “Powerful”
articles.summary: If you walked away from the StarCraft reveal excited for the franchise to return, but unsure what this new game even is, you're not alone. Aside from being described during the BlizzCon Opening Ceremony as an open-world shooter, Blizzard didn't share much else.
body: The StarCraft franchise, having taken the form of real-time strategy games previously, has typically used an isometric perspective. When it came to choosing what perspective to offer in the new shooter, it sounds like it wasn't a difficult decision.

"Oh, that's easy," Hay said when GameSpot asked him about whether StarCraft will be a first- or third-person game. "I want to be able to see my armor. First thing we did is we built it, put it on a turntable, and spun it around like, 'Ah, awesome, cool!' I want to be able to see it, so third-person, right?

"That doesn't mean that we don't have the license to, in a couple of spaces, do a little bit different and whatnot, but third-person: You get to see your armor, you get to see the full weight of everything you have, and then you get to see stuff that's in my head that I can't tell you."
points: If you walked away from the StarCraft reveal excited for the franchise to return, but unsure what this new game even is, you're not alone.
Aside from being described during the BlizzCon Opening Ceremony as an open-world shooter, Blizzard didn't share much else.

articles.title: StarCraft Reboot Is “Focusing On Single-Player,” Creative Director Says
articles.summary: StarCraft is "focusing on single-player," StarCraft creative director and general manager Dan Hay and associate manager of development operations Anna Lee Hertling said in an interview with GameSpot.
body: One of the biggest announcements of BlizzCon 2026 was the return of StarCraft, described as an open-world shooter and slated for a 2030 release. Aside from its impressive reveal cinematic, there wasn't much additional information about how StarCraft would play or what the shooter reboot of the RTS franchise would entail.
Now, we have some more details. When asked whether StarCraft would be single-player or co-op, Hay said the team is "focusing on single player."

"We are focused right now on the conversation of focusing on single-player, focusing on that Marine fantasy, and then making sure that we think about what it is to be that character," Hay said. "That's what we're saying for now."

He said players will play as a named character that can "build a reputation and a rapport" with other in-game characters. He said the game's story will have a beginning, middle, and an "end," and that Blizzard wants it to feel like a "boxed product." Thought it's story will have an end, Hay said Blizzard wants the game to be one players can visit, explore, leave, and come back to.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever Officially Brings Gamepad Controls Blizzard's MMO
articles.summary: One of the biggest surprises from BlizzCon 2026 was Blizzard's reveal of World of Warcraft Forever, a new version of the long-running massively multiplayer online role-playing game that will give adventurers a new type of classic experience.
body: Blizzard had another World of Warcraft Forever surprise on the show floor: The MMO is playable on a gamepad, the first time that World of Warcraft has received such robust, official game controller support. Typically, the game is played with a keyboard and mouse — and a series of keybindings for spells and actions. We played World of Warcraft Forever ourselves with a gamepad, and it works surprisingly well.
But don't count on World of Warcraft Forever coming to consoles or handheld PCs any time soon. That's not really the goal of gamepad support in Forever, the game's developers tell Polygon.

"We’ve been thinking about World of Warcraft Forever as a third pillar of World of Warcraft," said Nora Valletta, lead software engineer on the game. "There's so much that we're delivering here, it felt like an opportunity for us to explore all manner of ideas, not just on gameplay front, but also how do players interface with our game?"

articles.summary: Thanks to rumors and reports, the announcement of a new StarCraft game taking the form of an open-world shooter did not come as a complete surprise at BlizzCon's Opening Ceremony. What is surprising is when it's coming: 2030.
body: Hay said that with Blizzard being confident in what it's developed so far, it didn't want to further delay going public and getting the benefit of putting it in front of fans.

"There's a moment when you're making a game where you're like, 'Have we landed the emotion? Do we feel like we have enough of the verve, the identity, and the feel of it to start to share it?'" Hay continued. "About a year ago, we started to feel like we were there, so we were like, 'Okay, it's time to show it. It's time to get feedback.'

"What's super important about it is you want to put it out there, get people to feel the emotion and the value of it, and you want to be there live to be able to get a sense of how they feel about it. We were in the room; it felt great. People were going nuts."

articles.title: Blizzard Has No Plans To Turn Battle.net Into A Steam Competitor
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red confirmed at BlizzCon that both The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 will come to Battle.net, Blizzard's proprietary game storefront, before the end of the year.
body: Battle.net predates Steam, having launched in 1997 alongside the original Diablo as a platform for player chats and listings of multiplayer servers. Over time, it became the hub for buying Blizzard (and only Blizzard) games on PC. Things stayed that way until Destiny 2 launched on the service in 2017. In the years since, other Activision-published series like Call of Duty and Crash Bandicoot made their way to Battle.net as well.

Following Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, Xbox Game Studios and Bethesda titles like Avowed, Sea of Thieves, The Outer Worlds 2, and Doom: The Dark Ages also made their way to Battle.net. Now that CD Projekt Red games are coming to Battle.net, you'd be remiss not to wonder if we should expect a flood of other third-party titles to come in the future.
Despite this trend, Blizzard's Andrew Guerrero quickly made it clear during a BlizzCon interview with Polygon that Blizzard has no ambition of taking on the likes of Steam.
points: CD Projekt Red confirmed at BlizzCon that both The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 will come to Battle.net, Blizzard's proprietary game storefront, before the end of the year.

articles.title: 14 Years Later, TNT's Criminally Overlooked Action Series Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: Looking back, the late 2000s marked a short, largely unsung golden age for quirky TV antiheroes. It was like every showrunner in Los Angeles tuned in to a marathon of The Saint around the same time, which led to a short but memorable fascination with crime-fighting criminals.
body: This was the heyday of shows about spies, thieves, and con men, who were all forced into using their skills to deal with worse crooks than themselves. For whatever reason, most of these ran on the USA Network, such as White Collar, Burn Notice, and Psych, but one of the best ran for five seasons on TNT.

That was Leverage, a weekly heist show about a crew of master criminals recruited for targeted scams against the rich and powerful. It's been a cult favorite for over a decade, but Leverage has also been notoriously hard to find in syndication or on streaming platforms. Now all but Leverage ’s most recent season has been made available for free on YouTube via ElectricNOW, the official channel of its production company Electric Entertainment.

Leverage begins with Nate Ford (Timothy Hutton), who used to be an insurance investigator. When Nate's own company refused to cover a treatment that could've saved his son's life, Nate quit the business.
points: Looking back, the late 2000s marked a short, largely unsung golden age for quirky TV antiheroes.

articles.title: Diablo 5 will fully support multiplayer, but Blizzard won't say how similar to Diablo 4 it'll be
articles.summary: Diablo 5 may be set in a lonely world ravaged by a demon lord, but you'll still be able to team up with your friends like in previous Diablo games. Senior game director Joe Shely confirmed that Diablo 5 will fully support multiplayer in a group interview with PC Gamer: "Like Diablo 4, it is a game…
body: Specific details about multiplayer, like if you can run into other players in the open world like you can in Diablo 4's endgame, weren't mentioned. Blizzard said that information will have to wait until we're closer to its 2029 release.

One of the biggest changes that differentiates Diablo 5 from Diablo 4 is its return to having a procedurally-generated overworld and dungeons. This is supposed to convey the shifting nature of the world as you travel across the continent with your caravan cleansing it of Diablo's corruption. It's possible that this might dramatically change how you'll interact with other players once you're finished with the campaign, especially if everyone experiences their own version of Sanctuary.

Running into a bunch of other players might ruin the illusion that you're a lone hero fighting back against the forces of Hell. Blizzard says Diablo 5 will incorporate a lot of things it learned from Diablo 4, but it's unclear if that will include things like world events and bosses. Diablo 4 is also overflowing with skins and cosmetics that, if carried forward, would suggest there must be some way of showing off your fit to the other heroes of Sanctuary.

articles.title: Diablo 5 Has A Surprising Connection To Dragon Age
articles.summary: While Diablo 5 has made a big splash at BlizzCon 2026, some role-playing game fans may have missed the pedigree of some of its developers. Not only are series stalwarts like game director Joe Shely and production director Tiffany Wat working on the follow-up to Diablo 4, a notable former BioWare…
body: That's great news for Dragon Age fans, who will get another taste of Hepler's narrative work in 2029.

Hepler was previously a senior writer at BioWare, where she contributed heavily to the first three Dragon Age video games. In particular, Hepler really fleshed out the dwarven side of Thedas and many of Dragon Age 2 and Dragon Age: Inquisition 's most beloved characters. If you enjoy the writing and characters of the original Dragon Age trilogy, her involvement with Diablo 5 makes the game's narrative potential much more interesting.

While Dragon Age 2 is fondly remembered nowadays, at the time of the game's release, players did not take kindly to the sequel's reduced scope and issues with the combat. Shortly after Dragon Age 2's release, comments made by Hepler years prior about combat in video games were weaponized by online provocateurs, who tried to pin Dragon Age 2's biggest flaws on Hepler's involvement.

body: Wouldn't it be nice if more of Blizzard's classic games were available on Steam? People could easily play them on their Steam Decks! But no, that's not happening. Instead, we're getting Cyberpunk 2077 on Battle.net.

After announcing at GamesCom that The Witcher 3's upcoming remastered version would release on Battle.net as well as the expected platforms, Blizzard and CD Projekt have announced at BlizzCon that Cyberpunk 2077 and its expansion will release there later this year. articles.title: 10 big World of Warcraft Forever details from BlizzCon: No separate realms, optional transmog, and massively improved items
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever might be stuck in the first year of the MMO for the foreseeable future, but it's going to draw from future iterations of it to freshen up the experience.
body: Blizzard held a panel at BlizzCon today where WoW Forever developers dug into the crucial design changes that will differentiate it from the WoW Classic we already have. This version of the MMO doesn't sound like it'll be as much of a grind as the OG with its revised classes, talent trees, and all-new mechanics for pulling strangers together in the open world.

Many of the changes seem to fill in the gaps of the original WoW experience so that there's several things to chase as you explore Azeroth. Developers broke down how the MMO will bring players together, how the new "Legacy" progression system works, and how new and old items will influence combat.

There are a lot more details, especially for how popular abilities will work, explained in the panel. Part of the goal, Blizzard said, was to "unsolve" the game and give players a reason to experiment again.

It won't be a long wait to see how it all comes together. WoW Forever will launch on November 4 and will be playable under the same subscription as regular WoW. A beta will go live on Thursday, September 17, which you can access by purchasing the game early.
points: World of Warcraft Forever might be stuck in the first year of the MMO for the foreseeable future, but it's going to draw from future iterations of it to freshen up the experience.

body: A critically acclaimed game to be sure, but there are technical issues to address in the PC version of The Blood of Dawnwalker - from its somewhat optimistic recommended specs to the intrusive stutter we noted even on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D paired with an RTX 5090. Rebel Wolves suggests that an upscaled 1440p at 60fps is possible on an Nvidia RTX 4060 - but we don't quite agree, so to what extent can optimised settings make a difference?
